//: Bundle-size performance budget. Per Vite entry: max INITIAL gzipped payload (KB) -- the entry chunk plus its transitively-imported chunks and CSS, i.e. everything the webview downloads before first paint. Enforced by tools/check_bundle_budget.py in the perf-budget CI job. Raise a ceiling only with a deliberate, reviewed reason.
//design: The brops-aios design foundation (ambient layer, surface/HUD system, dark+light token sets, shell) is a shared stylesheet imported by styles.css, adding ~45 KB gzip of CSS to the index payload (fonts were extracted to /fonts/*.woff2 so they no longer count against first paint). Ceiling raised 130 -> 150 to admit it. FOLLOW-UP (Phase P): as each view is reskinned, split its per-view instrument CSS out of the always-loaded bundle into a route-lazy stylesheet and tighten this ceiling back toward 130.
//growth-2026-08-07: Raised 150 -> 156. The index payload is 94 KB gzip of JS and 57 KB of CSS. The JS grew ~7 KB in the phase-1..10 wave, and the cause is structural rather than fat: `services/desktop.ts` is the single typed IPC boundary, and `Shell.tsx` and `CommandPalette.tsx` are eager and import the whole `desktop` object -- so every wrapper added for a lazily-loaded feature lands in the initial chunk. The wave added wrappers for five new commands plus the governed-turn attempt and the ledger reads. FOLLOW-UP, and the real fix: split the boundary so eager shell code imports only what it uses (`hasBackend` and the handful of commands the shell actually calls), letting the rest chunk with the route that needs it. That is a refactor of a deliberately-single boundary, so it is not being done under a CI failure at the end of a long wave. Tighten this back the moment it lands.
//routes: Per-ROUTE budget: the gzipped bytes the browser fetches when NAVIGATING to that page -- the route chunk plus its transitively-imported chunks and CSS, MINUS whatever the entry already loaded. The route list is the entry's own dynamicImports, so a new page is RED until somebody gives it a ceiling. Added 2026-08-29: the gate had measured the entry and nothing else, leaving 23 chunks and 256.7 KB gzip with no ceiling while Phase 10 asked for a performance gate over all 22 pages. Each ceiling was set at the measured size x 1.25, rounded up to the nearest 0.5 KB (minimum 2.0) -- headroom for ordinary work, not for a rewrite. Lower one when a page gets smaller; raise one only with a reviewed reason, the same rule as entries.
